Additional diagnostic tests.notes: Excludes significant CAD or ACS in clinically suspected myocarditis.
For diagnosis and indication to specific treatment (see Table 32).
May be useful in patients who cannot undergo CMR or with suspected systemic autoimmune disease or cardiac sarcoidosis.

notes: Skeletal muscle enzymes, liver and renal function, natriuretic peptides, thyroid function tests, iron status, markers of systemic autoimmune disease.
PCR testing of common cardiotrophic viruses: can detect systemic infection but does not prove cardiac infection and cannot substitute viral genome analysis on EMB samples.
Circulating IgG antibodies to cardiotrophic viruses are common in the absence of viral myocarditis; very limited diagnostic usefulness.
Specific test for SARS-CoV-2, Borrelia, HIV or CMV if clinical suspicion.

content.Definition of suspected acute myocarditi: Clinical presentation + ≥1 mandatory diagnostic test being positive (by preference CMR) in the absence of significant coronary artery, valvular or congenital heart disease, or other causes.

Clinical presentation.description: Acute/new onset chest pain, dyspnoea, signs of left and/or right heart failure, and/or unexplained arrhythmias or aborted sudden death.

ECG.description: New and dynamic ST-T abnormalities, including pseudo-infarct ST segment elevation, atrial or ventricular arrhythmias, AV blocks, QRS abnormalities.
